q: Which products must carry a BEE star label, and which are voluntary?
title: BEE star label: mandatory vs voluntary
short: Eleven products need a BEE star label by law, including distribution transformers, room ACs, ceiling fans, LED lamps and refrigerators. Industrial motors, pumps, air compressors, diesel generators and chillers are still voluntary, so an unlabelled one is legal but tells you less.
audience: Factory buyers, procurement teams and equipment makers

ul: Frost free refrigerator and direct cool refrigerator.
Room air conditioners: variable speed, fixed speed, and cassette, floor standing, ceiling and corner units.
Tubular fluorescent lamps and LED lamps.
Solid state inverters, solar water heaters and Li-ion traction batteries.

sections.h: What this means when you buy
p: For voluntary products, ask for the star label or the test data behind it. BEE accepts test reports only from accredited labs, and there is no negative tolerance on star bands, so a labelled model must meet its band when check tested.

senseible: Senseible reads equipment invoices onto your Scope 3 trail and electricity bills into Scope 2, so the effect of a higher-star purchase shows up in metered kWh rather than on the label alone.
